title: Orange Triangle Ahead
hook: Orange triangle ahead in the cones. You are doing thirty.
scene: Heavy rain at night on a Kent work zone, cones still in the lane. In the cone line, a farm tractor from somebody's last run south, no Grange, just one machine, orange slow-vehicle triangle dirty but lit by your lamps. It is doing twelve. You are doing thirty because the insulin clock got loud in your head. The triangle is the sign. Pass on a two-lane with no sightline and you are in his blind spot and oncoming's. The cones make it worse. Your left blinker already wants out.
decision: The slow-moving triangle is ahead in the cones. Do you pass?

options.text: Pass now — twelve is not a speed and the insulin is not a suggestion
options.result: You pull out in the rain. The tractor occupies more width than it looks. Oncoming is a pair of lamps you did not have. You dive back in and clip a cone. The triangle fills your glass. You saved nothing and spent a lot of noise.

options.text: Flash him to pull into the cones so you can go
options.result: The flash hits the triangle and comes back at you twice as bright. He has nowhere to pull. He brakes. You almost eat the hitch of a machine that cannot get out of your way because you asked it to.

options.text: Stay behind, drop to his twelve, and wait for a marked passing zone with sight
options.result: You lift to twelve. The cone line ends. A painted passing zone appears with a sightline you can actually see. You take it then, clean, and leave him a gap. The insulin is still cold. Twelve cost you a minute. A pass in the rain would have cost the run.

options.text: Go around on the gravel because the lane is his
options.result: The gravel is a ditch in the rain. The tires climb and the plow drops. You are beside him in a trench with no legal lane. He never saw you. The first thing he knows is your roof in his left mirror and a sound like a drum.

debrief: An orange triangle marks a machine doing farm speed. Pass only where the paint allows it and you can see. Twelve cost you a minute.

source.teaching_target: The orange triangle marks a slow vehicle; pass only where passing is legal and sight distance is enough.

image_brief.subject: the rear of a worn farm tractor filling the windshield mesh; a dirty orange slow-moving-vehicle triangle is bolted to the tractor's back, centered, lit by the headlights
image_brief.foreground: worn black steering wheel and cracked faded pink dash; rain on the glass; welded steel mesh
image_brief.midground: the tractor's rear tires and hitch; the SMV triangle fastened to the machine, not on the ground; orange work-zone cones left and right of the lane
image_brief.background: a two-lane Kent work zone at night, heavy rain, a dark shop building, no oncoming lamps yet
image_brief.read: the orange triangle is fastened to the tractor — this machine is doing farm speed

geometry.ego_nose_in_frame: the plow blade points toward the tractor
